scenario: annual IT support contract for a 3-branch clinic chain

seller.product: Annual IT support contract (helpdesk, onsite SLA, resident engineer, backups, network) for Arogyam Family Clinics
price_list: Proposal: ₹6.8 lakh per year + GST, up to 50 endpoints, resident engineer 3 days a week
Critical SLA: remote pickup 15 minutes, onsite 4 hours; non-critical next business day
Parts excluded: procured at cost + 10% handling; labour included

speakers.name: Rahul Menon
speakers.style: account manager, polite, eager to close, concedes a little fast, recovers well

speakers.name: Dr. Anjali Venkatesh
speakers.style: founder and senior doctor, busy, decisive, sharp on value

speakers.name: Prakash Iyer
speakers.style: admin and finance manager, meticulous, reads every line, hard negotiator

speakers.name: Sneha Pillai
speakers.style: seller's service delivery lead, calm, precise on SLA terms

coaching_truths.statement: Rahul conceded ₹40,000 (₹6.8 lakh to ₹6.4 lakh) the moment he heard the competitor number, before asking what that quote covered; the founder read it as a sign of more room.
He then asked what the TechSaathi quote included and compared it against their own outage: 8-hour response, no Sunday cover, no resident engineer.
He said hardware replacement was included, then corrected it to labour only, with parts at cost plus 10%.
He cut Prakash off with a track-record claim when Prakash asked about SLA penalties; Prakash had to insist on finishing.
Later concessions were traded, not given: ₹6.1 lakh for a two-year term and quarterly advance, ₹5.95 lakh with director approval, and the free DR drill to close the backup worry.
The founder said a fourth clinic opens by Holi; Rahul only congratulated her and did not offer to add it to the contract or price it.
